title: Model weights rolling refresh and local cache sizing recommendations
author: Ava Moreno
body:
Summary:
This document provides an operator-focused playbook for safely performing rolling refreshes of model weight artifacts and for sizing the local model-weights cache on on-prem / air-gapped private deployments. It covers goals, risk model, telemetry and SLOs, a step-by-step rolling update procedure, sizing guidelines and worked examples, rollback triggers, and verification checks for day-2 operations.

Intended audience:
- Field operators and site reliability engineers responsible for private deployments
- Release engineers coordinating model artifact updates
- Support engineers validating customer acceptance after a refresh

Why this matters:
Model weight refreshes (new model versions, quantized artifacts, or security-patched artifacts) are high-impact operations for private deployments. Improper refreshes can cause repeated cold-starts, evict critical KV cache entries, and cause tail-latency regressions. A carefully controlled rolling refresh plus conservative local cache sizing reduces customer-visible disruptions while still allowing frequent model updates.

Goals and constraints:
- Goal: Replace weights with minimal 99th-percentile latency regression (<10% relative) and no more than 1% sustained error-rate increase per tenant during the operation.
- Constraint: Limited local disk and memory on edge appliances; intermittent upstream connectivity for air-gapped refreshes.
- Safety: Any automated step must be reversible; manual approval gates for major-architecture swaps (e.g., FP16->quantized INT8).

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments / Field Operations (oncall: private-deploy-ops).
- Release owner: model-onboarding team (contact: model-release@redwood.example.com).
- Escalation path: operator -> field-ops lead -> SRE -> oncall product-eng. See related_pages for contact pages.

Telemetry and SLOs to monitor before, during, and after refresh:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for inference calls per tenant and per route.
- Error rate: HTTP 5xx and application-level model failures (tokenization/decoding errors).
- Cold-starts per minute: number of new model-container initializations.
- Disk pressure: % used of weights-cache mount; inode exhaustion.
- Memory pressure: RSS and OOM events on runtime processes.
- Avail: service healthy checks and per-model readiness probes.
SLO thresholds used by operators: p99 increase <10% (relative), error-rate delta <1% absolute, cold-start rate <3/min per node during steady state.

Local model-weights cache sizing recommendations (summary table):
- Small footprint sites (single-rack, latency-sensitive dev sites): allocate 2x working-set weights on disk, 1x working-set in RAM for memory-mapped access.
- Medium sites (2–8 GPU nodes): allocate 1.5x working-set on disk, 0.75x working-set in RAM.
- Large sites (>=8 GPU nodes, multi-tenant): allocate 1.2x working-set on disk, 0.5x working-set in RAM and rely on shared NFS/central storage for cold artifacts.

Sizing table (worked example):
| Site class | Typical concurrent models | Per-model artifact size | Working set (models) | Disk buffer | Recommended disk cache | Recommended RAM for mmap | Notes |
| Small | 1–3 | 18 GB | 2 | 36 GB | 72 GB | 18 GB | Single-rack dev / proof-of-concept |
| Medium | 4–16 | 18 GB | 6 | 36 GB | 108 GB | 12 GB | Production pilot clusters |
| Large | 16+ | 18–140 GB | 10 | 40 GB | 220 GB | 30–60 GB | Multi-tenant with varied model sizes |

Sizing formula (operators):
- estimated_working_set = sum(peak_concurrent_models_expected * per_model_size)
- disk_cache = round_up(estimated_working_set * disk_multiplier + disk_buffer)
- ram_mmap = round_up(estimated_working_set * ram_multiplier)
Suggested multipliers: disk_multiplier = 1.2 (large) to 2.0 (small), ram_multiplier = 0.5 (large) to 1.0 (small).

Preflight checklist (required):
1) Validate artifact integrity: verify PGP signature and checksum of model artifact bundle.
2) Confirm storage availability: free_space >= disk_cache + 10% slack.
3) Confirm runtime compatibility: artifact schema vX <= supported_runtime_schema_vY.
4) Snapshot existing state: collect KV-cache manifests, running container PID lists, and model readiness endpoints.
5) Scheduling window: confirm maintenance window and stakeholder notification.
6) Rollback plan: pre-stage previous artifact and test local restore on a non-production node.

Rolling refresh procedure (safe-by-default, minimal disruption):
1) Stage artifacts to a central staging bucket accessible to nodes (airgap: ship via OTA bundle and verification script).
2) On each node, in a staggered sequence (one node every N minutes depending on cluster size), perform: 
   a) Pause new model placements: set cluster routing weight to 0 for node (or cordon node in k8s).
   b) Drain in-flight requests: wait for active_request_count == 0 or timeout (recommended 30s–90s).
   c) Fetch && verify artifact bundle: verify checksum + signature.
   d) Place artifact into local weights cache under a new versioned directory (do not overwrite in-place).
   e) Restart model runtime process with versioned artifact path (graceful reload path preferred to full restart).
   f) Run smoke tests: send sample prompts (happy path + 2 regression prompts) and validate outputs and latency.
   g) If smoke tests pass, reintroduce node to routing pool (uncordon) and monitor for 10 minutes for tail-latency regressions.
   h) If smoke tests fail or tail latency spikes > p99 threshold, trigger automatic rollback for that node.
3) Continue sequence across nodes until zero nodes remain on old version.
4) Post-refresh validation: run tenant-level synthetic workloads for 30–60 minutes and verify telemetry targets.

Commands and examples (kubernetes-based appliance example):
- Cordon node: kubectl cordon <node-name>
- Drain: kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
- Install artifact (example): /opt/redwood/bin/install_weights.sh --bundle /staging/model-v2.bundle --dest /var/lib/redwood/weights/model-v2 --verify
- Restart runtime: systemctl restart redwood-runtime.service
- Smoke test example (curl): curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/predict -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' | jq '.latency_ms, .status'

Rollback and failure modes:
- Node-level rollback: if smoke tests fail, restore previous symlinked artifact and run graceful-reload; if reload not supported, restart runtime with previous binary.
- Cluster-level rollback: if systemic regression is observed across >25% of nodes, immediately stop rolling updates, mark release as suspect, and coordinate a cluster rollback via the release owner.
- Eviction storms: if disk pressure causes weights eviction during refresh, pause rollout and increase disk cache or reduce resident working set by temporarily reducing model placements.

Operational safety knobs and runtime flags:
- preload_on_start: boolean (true recommended) — preload weights into mmap to avoid high-latency first requests.
- mmap_prefault_pages: integer — number of pages to prefault at startup to reduce first-request tail latency (default 0; 65536 for high-memory nodes).
- max_concurrent_reload: integer — limit concurrent reloads on a node to avoid OOM.
- background_eviction_threshold_pct: 75 — start background eviction only above this disk usage to avoid premature churn.

Verification and acceptance tests (post-refresh):
1) Acceptance synthetic suite (provided by model-onboarding): pass rate >= 99/100 prompts.
2) Latency: p99 not exceed pre-release baseline by >10%.
3) Resource stability: no OOMs; no sustained CPU > 85% for >5 minutes.
4) Telemetry: ensure logs include "weights:loaded:OK" per node in the last 5 minutes.

Operational tips and lessons learned from field installs:
- Never overwrite existing weight directories in-place; use versioned directories and atomically switch symlinks. This avoids partial artifact corruption on interruption.
- Prefer graceful reload hooks over full process restart to retain warmed KV-caches where possible.
- For air-gapped sites, include a small bootstrap agent that can verify and stage bundles offline; operators reported a 40% reduction in human errors when using a signed bundle installer.

Appendix A: Example artifact layout on node:
/var/lib/redwood/weights/
  model-v1/ (sha256-abc...)
  model-v2/ (sha256-def...)
  current -> model-v1

Appendix B: Quick checklist for small sites (1–3 nodes):
- Pre-copy bundle to all nodes via scp; verify checksums locally.
- Stagger refresh with 30–60s between nodes.
- Keep a local fallback copy of previous artifact on each node for immediate rollback.

Appendix C: Contact and reference links:
- Model release playbook: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/operator-handback-and-custodian-rollforward-playbook-2026
- KV-cache migration guide: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/kv-cache-migrations-and-runtime-state-migration-playbook-2025

If you discover gaps or want this procedure automated in the operator toolkit, open a PR against infra-operator-scripts and tag eng-private-deployments@redwood.example.com.
